rationale: Upstream directory layout is preserved deliberately. A uid is built from the file path, so include/fmt/os.h and src/os.cc are distinct modules — flattening the fixture put them in one directory and manufactured 14 header/source uid collisions that do not exist in the real repository. Keep the subdirectories. C++ has a genuinely low ceiling and this floor is deliberately not near 1.0. tree-sitter has no preprocessor, so every unexpandable macro is a token the grammar must guess at, and fmt is macro-dense (FMT_BEGIN_NAMESPACE, FMT_CONSTEXPR, FMT_API, gtest's TEST). Almost every uncaptured named function is stranded behind a compound_statement or ERROR in its ancestor chain — the enclosing namespace or class failed to parse and collapsed into a bare block, so the function survives but its scope does not. Emitting entities for them was rejected: the name is recoverable but the qualified name is not, and a Callable with a wrong qn resolves to the wrong target rather than to nothing. Their calls are still recovered, because _extract_calls descends into that debris and attributes to the nearest scope that did survive (ADR-0031). The full 72-file checkout scores named_funcs 0.690 / calls 0.937 / duplicate_uids 116, so this fixture tracks it closely on all three. The 7.6% call shortfall is dominated by C++ named casts (static_cast/reinterpret_cast/const_cast/dynamic_cast), which the grammar shapes exactly like calls but which are keywords, not callables — an edge to one could never resolve; the rest is calls with no static callee name at all (fp[i](), (*fp)(), chained f()()). ROUTING: .h is shared between C and C++ and is now routed by sniffing the content (sniff_header_is_cpp), not by the extension alone. This replaced the earlier note here that the routing bug was unfixed — it is fixed. Measured against 583 real C headers from CPython 3.14, Python 3.13 and site-packages, the sniff flips 13, and every one of those genuinely contains C++ inside an #ifdef __cplusplus block (pyatomic_std.h's `extern "C++"`, mimalloc's STL allocator, dynamic_annotations.h's `template <class T>`, PyWin32's COM headers): zero flips on a header that is C-only. Against fmt's 25 headers it flips 23; the two it leaves are correct — fmt-c.h is fmt's actual C API header, and core.h contains nothing but #includes. Comments and string literals are blanked before matching, because in CPython every mention of `class` or `namespace` outside those dual-language headers is prose; and each marker demands syntactic context, because C reserves none of these words and CPython really does ship a `namespaceSeparator` field. DUPLICATE UIDS: 11 -> 49 (the .h routing fix, which made 100 more Callables visible in this fixture, 212 to 312, and C++ overloading means more entities on one name) -> 6 (ATL-107 / ADR-0032). An overloaded name takes its signature into the uid, and only an overloaded one does: a name declared once in its scope keeps the uid it always had, which is what bounds the churn to what was already ambiguous. The suffix is <template params>(<parameter types>)<trailing cv/ref qualifiers> -- everything C++ resolves an overload on and nothing it does not, so file::dup2(int) and file::dup2(int,error_code&) separate, basic_scan_arg's nine constructors separate, and value()& / value()const& separate. noexcept is excluded because C++ does not overload on it and a header that spells it where the definition does not would split one function in two. Namespace qualifiers and whitespace are stripped so the suffix reads as source rather than as a linker symbol; a parameter pack renders [] rather than ..., because a dot in a qualified_name separates scope segments and an ellipsis would manufacture two fake ones (jvm.py renders Java varargs the same way, for the same reason). The overload set is computed per scope over a view that flattens #ifdef arms, extern "C" blocks and template <...> wrappers, so a set split across a conditional-compilation boundary is still one set -- and the scope is whatever encloses the declaration, not just a class body: detail::read (8 overloads) and scan_to (3) are namespace- and translation-unit-level. THE REMAINING 6 are three shapes, none of which a signature suffix can address. (1) FOUR are the header/source pairs ADR-0032 accepts and records: a member declared in test/gtest-extra.h and defined out-of-line in test/gtest-extra.cc beside it produces the same module qualified name, and merging them is arguably right since they are one function. Preserving them was a check, not an accident -- neither side is overloaded in its own file, so neither takes a suffix. (2) ONE is convert_rwcount(size_t), defined identically in the #ifdef _WIN32 and #elif FMT_USE_FCNTL arms of src/os.cc. Both arms are walked deliberately, because which one compiles depends on a build configuration the indexer does not have; the two signatures are identical, so no signature-derived uid can separate them. (3) ONE is a parse artifact, not an overload: include/fmt/os.h declares `FMT_API ~buffered_file() noexcept;` and tree-sitter, having no preprocessor, absorbs FMT_API as the return type and leaves the `~` as an ERROR node -- so the destructor arrives named `buffered_file` with an empty parameter list and collides with the default constructor. The entity is misnamed rather than ambiguous, and recovering it is a separate fix. KNOWN LIMIT, pinned in test_out_of_line_definitions_are_weighed_against_their_own_scope: a class body and the file scope holding an out-of-line definition are two scopes, so a member defined once outside a class that declares two overloads of that name keeps its plain uid and stops merging with its own declaration. Two out-of-line definitions of one name in one file are still weighed against each other, which is the shape that occurs in practice (file::dup2). Closing it needs the set keyed per file rather than per scope, which costs a second walk of every function body (~+44% on C++ parse time, measured on fmt). The full 72-file checkout moves 492 -> 116 on the same change, with named_funcs and calls unmoved at 0.690 / 0.937 and the Callable count unmoved at 3440 -- this renames entities, it does not add or drop any. 166 of those 116 collisions' 221 entities sit in the single vendored 20k-line test/gtest/gmock-gtest-all.cc amalgamation, and split between the same #if-arm shape as convert_rwcount (GetThreadCount has 8 platform arms) and out-of-line definitions of explicit template specializations (Matcher<const std::string&>::Matcher beside Matcher<std::string>::Matcher), which collapse onto one class name because _get_qualified_declarator_name strips template arguments from a scope by design, so that Box<T>::method still matches the TypeDef named Box. The rest are members whose enclosing class did not survive parsing and landed at file scope -- the same stranded-scope problem that caps named_funcs, where the name is right and the scope is not. One smaller gap is a scope mismatch this change could have closed and did not: a friend function is named in the enclosing namespace but counted in the class body that declares it, so friends in two different classes are two overload sets rather than one (fmt's test/std-test.cc my_nso::format_as, 3 entities, 2 duplicates).
